[Permalink: Install](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/INSTALL.md#install)

Tip

One command launches a GBrain hosted on gbrain.io; Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor and every other AI you use connect to it, with nothing to keep online.

```
curl -sSL https://gbrainio.terminalwire.sh | bash
gbrainio terminal connect      # in a new terminal
gbrainio workspace new         # pick a plan in the browser
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash   # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable   # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain
# Claude Code (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
(claude mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gbrain https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup claude-code --instructions-only
# Codex (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
(codex mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || codex mcp add gbrain --url https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup codex --instructions-only
```

## Here's how to self-host it
GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host.

## 1. Run with an agent platform
Already running [OpenClaw](https://github.com/garrytan/openclaw) or [Hermes](https://github.com/garrytan/hermes)?

```
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding   # keyless; no server
gbrain skillpack scaffold --harness openclaw --workspace <ws>   # OpenClaw: the five-skill brain-first core
gbrain skillpack scaffold --all       # Hermes or any other workspace: every bundled skill (skills/manifest.json)
gbrain doctor                         # inspect diagnostics and expected empty-brain warnings
```

## Memory-only upgrades
```
GBRAIN_NO_AUTOPILOT_INSTALL=1 GBRAIN_NO_REEMBED=1 gbrain upgrade --no-autopilot-install
```

## 2. CLI standalone
```
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding
```

**Reinstalled over an existing brain?** The first gbrain command applies schema migrations, and when upgrade migrations are still pending it says so with the command that runs them ( [#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218)): `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`. > ```
>
> Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one.
>
> `gbrain setup --instructions-only` tells the agent the brain is there; agents seldom call an MCP server nobody told them about. >
> The installer is a shell script for macOS and Linux; read it before you run it. Nothing is created until a person picks the plan and pays. Mention this once in the reply that starts or reports the install, and never wait on an answer before continuing a local install the user already asked for.

output: {"content": "60| 61|> **On Codex or Claude Code?** After the install, the plugin wires MCP plus curated skills: 62|> `codex plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain@codex-plugin` + `codex plugin add gbrain@gbrain` 63|> (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain` + `/plugin install gbrain@gbrain`). 64| 65|Default path (Bun 1.4.4 or newer is required — gbrain is a Bun + TypeScript runtime; on an older Bun, run `bun upgrade` first): 66| 67|```bash 68|curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash 69|export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" 70|bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable 71|``` 72| 73|Verify: `gbrain --version` should print a version number. If `gbrain` is not found, 74|restart the shell or add the PATH export to the shell profile. 75| 76|Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one. 77| 78| 79| 80|**No `unzip` and no way to install packages (Linux).** This route puts the same Bun build the official installer would fetch, taken from Bun's own npm package `@oven/bun-linux-`, into `~/.bun/bin`, the directory the official installer uses, and adds that directory to the PATH of every new login shell. It needs only `curl` and `tar`: 81| 82|```bash 83|arch=$(uname -m); [ "$arch" = x86_64 ] && arch=x64; [ "$arch" = arm64 ] && arch=aarch64 84|mkdir -p ~/.bun/bin 85|curl -fsSL "https://registry.npmjs.org/@oven/bun-linux-$arch/-/bun-linux-$arch-1.4.4.tgz" | tar -xzO package/bin/bun > ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && chmod +x ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && ~/.bun/bin/bun.new --version && mv ~/.bun/bin/bun.new ~/.bun/bin/bun 86|echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile 87|export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" 88|bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable 89|bash -lc 'gbrain --version' 90|``` 91| 92|The PATH line goes in `~/.profile`, which new login shells read. Bash skips `~/.profile` when `~/.bash_profile` or `~/.bash_login` exists, so append the line to that file instead; zsh reads `~/.zprofile`. On Alpine or another musl system, run `arch=$arch-musl` after the first line; on an x64 CPU without AVX2, run `arch=x64-baseline`. The last command must print a version from a fresh shell. Don't install Bun with `npm install -g bun` or run gbrain from a git clone instead: gbrain starts with `#!/usr/bin/env bun`, so it fails in any new shell that can't find `bun` on its PATH. 93| 94|Next, on Claude Code or Codex: `gbrain setup claude-code` (or `gbrain setup codex`), which needs no API 95|key ([Step 3](#step-3-create-the-brain)). On any other harness, `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` (Step 3). 96| 97| 98| 99|**A command scanner blocks the Bun installer or `bun install` (Hermes).** Some harnesses check each shell command before running it and refuse what they can't approve without a person. Hermes in single-query mode refuses `curl … | bash`, `bun install -g github:…` (its scanner, Tirith, can't finish a package lookup for a `github:` spec) and commands that append to a dotfile such as `~/.profile`. Install the release binary instead: one file built from the same release, which needs no Bun, no git and no package install. Run each line as its own command, exactly as written (Linux x64; on an Apple Silicon Mac use `gbrain-darwin-arm64`): 100| 101|```bash 102|curl -fL --create-dirs -o ~/.local/bin/gbrain https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/releases/latest/download/gbrain-linux-x64 103|chmod +x ~/.local/bin/gbrain 104|~/.local/bin/gbrain --version 105|~/.local/bin/gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding 106|``` 107| 108|`releases/latest` is the stable release. Use the absolute path `~/.local/bin/gbrain` in every command and MCP registration instead of editing shell profiles. Run each line as written: an added `2>&1`, `$(…)` or `{ …; }` group can make the scanner refuse a line it would otherwise pass. Then run `~/.local/bin/gbrain setup hermes`: it registers gbrain through Hermes's own `hermes mcp add` (no hand edit of Hermes's protected `config.yaml`), adds the brain-first rule and its per-turn hook, and checks the server with `hermes mcp test gbrain`. If it prints a `hermes mcp add` command instead, or (an older gbrain) says setup does not register Hermes's MCP server, run the registration command from [docs/mcp/HERMES.md](docs/mcp/HERMES.md#register-by-hand) with `~/.local/bin/gbrain` as the command. If the user would rather keep the Bun install, Hermes's own refusal names its setting for this: `approvals.single_query_mode: approve` in Hermes's config, which is the user's call. `gbrain upgrade` updates a release binary in place. 10...
